items.title: Joe Darensbourg and Minor "Ram" Hall Interview, 1957-04-18
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Yeah. No, I figured that out myself. What was it, tennis? No, Aldo. Aldo.

ctx.x: It sounds fantastic now, but it's true. Yeah. They were all one to split. They wanted you to play. You, you, you, you, you was a big man when you hit one of those towns. Everybody wanted to see you. We played a little towns, like, uh, we played towns that guys had never heard a saxophone in person before. Never heard one. And the people in those little towns heard, heard much jazz before? No, no. Maybe once in a while. Some of the guys had left the town. We played towns that jazz had never come through, I mean…
Yeah. No, I figured that out myself. What was it, tennis? No, Aldo. Aldo.

The first time I picked up a saxophone, I could play it. Oh yeah? Yeah. But, also singing is quite different. From a clarinet? Yeah. Well, all, all saxophones, things are the same for that matter. But, uh, it's different from a clarinet. Still in all, if you can play a clarinet, you can play a saxophone. Something real easy, because the clarinet is a lot more difficult instrument than a saxophone. But I had, uh, and I had food with a saxophone before, a little bit, you know, because my teacher was a saxophone…
